美國理財顧問服務平台 Altruist 上週替旗下 AI 平台 Hazel 推出財務規劃 agent,把顧問原本要花好幾小時的六大財務規劃壓進幾分鐘——但真正該記下來的,是它「不做」的那件事。

Hazel 一次涵蓋退休、投資最佳化、現金流、遺產、稅務、保險與風險,六個過去往往要靠一整組專家分頭處理、動輒好幾小時的領域,現在幾分鐘就產出一份完整的財務規劃。

可是 Altruist 在中間畫了一條線。AI 只負責讀:財務文件、客戶會議、往來溝通紀錄,把客戶的狀況整理清楚。至於所有會印在規劃書上的數字,一律丟給專門的計算程式跑,不讓語言模型自己生。用他們的說法,每一個數字都是「被算出來的」,不是「被 AI 生成的」。

這條線,是今年金融 AI 最值得抄的一句話。AI 很會讀、很會整理、很會解釋;但只要是要負責任的數字,就得有一個能被回頭驗算的來源。

MarketDaily 走的是同一條線。AI 幫你把一整夜的財經新聞整理成一封信,週一到週六早上七點寄到你信箱;而我們把結算過的每一筆判斷都公開列在戰績頁上,輸的那些也留在上面,任何人都能自己回頭對。目前全功能限時免費開放;未來恢復收費後,現在訂閱的早鳥用戶永久保留免費使用權。

換你說說看:你比較願意用一個「什麼都幫你算好」的 AI,還是一個「敢告訴你數字從哪來」的 AI?在下面告訴我。

drafts.caption_en:
Last week Altruist — a US platform for financial advisors — shipped a financial planning agent inside its Hazel AI platform, squeezing six areas of planning that used to take advisors hours into a few minutes. But the part worth copying is what it refuses to do.

Hazel covers retirement, investment optimization, cash flow, estate, tax, and insurance and risk in one pass: six areas that a shop full of specialists used to work through over hours, now a comprehensive plan in minutes.

Except Altruist drew a line down the middle. The AI only reads — financial documents, client meetings, communications — and organizes the client's situation. Every number that ends up in the plan gets routed to dedicated calculation programs instead of being written by the language model. In their words, every figure is calculated, not AI-generated.

That line is the most quotable idea in finance AI this year. AI is great at reading, organizing and explaining. But any number you have to stand behind needs a source someone can go back and check.

MarketDaily runs on the same line. AI turns a whole night of financial news into one email that lands in your inbox at 7am Taipei time, Monday through Saturday; and every call we have settled is listed in the open on our track record page — the losing ones stay up too, so anyone can check for themselves. Everything is free for a limited time right now; when paid plans return, early subscribers keep free access forever.

Your turn: would you rather use an AI that does all the math for you, or one that tells you where the numbers came from? Tell me below.

Source: Altruist announcement, Aug 31, 2026.

翻完一份季報要一個下午,我現在 10 分鐘問完——差別不是我讀得比較快,是我不再從第一頁開始讀,而且只問三題。

先講最常見的錯:把財報丟給 AI 然後說「幫我總結」。摘要是它最會偷懶的地方,你會拿到一段誰都寫得出來的話。

換成這樣問。把財報(或法說會逐字稿)丟進去之後,直接複製這段:

「你手上這份是【公司名+哪一季】的財報。請照順序回答三題。每一題都要標出你引用的是哪一段、哪個報表欄位;找不到就直接說『這份文件裡沒有』,不要推測。
1. 這一季跟上一季比,哪三個數字變動最大?各是變好還是變壞,文件裡給的原因是什麼?
2. 管理層這次的用字,跟上一季比,哪裡變保守、哪裡變樂觀?把兩邊的原句都貼出來。
3. 這份文件裡最容易被略過、但可能對未來幾季不利的一段是什麼?為什麼?
最後補一句:要看到什麼,才代表第 3 題的疑慮成真、或者解除?」

為什麼這樣問有用,四個關鍵:
① 要它標出處 —— 編故事的成本變高,它得指得出某一段。
② 允許它說「文件裡沒有」 —— 這句最重要,你不給它承認不知道的空間,它就會編一個給你。
③ 問「跟上一季比,哪些字變了」 —— 語氣的轉彎通常比數字早出現,而這是人工比對最累、AI 最擅長的活。
④ 最後一題把結論變成可以被推翻的東西,不是一段讀後感。

三個提醒:
・它報的每個數字,回原始財報自己對一次,它照樣會編。
・只餵一季看不出趨勢,至少餵最近兩到三季再問第 1 題。
・這是幫你讀懂一家公司在說什麼,不是叫你買賣任何東西——它不知道你的成本,也不知道你打算放多久。

Reading a quarterly report cover to cover used to eat my whole afternoon. Now I am done in 10 minutes — not because I read faster, but because I stopped starting at page one and I only ask three questions.

The most common mistake first: dumping the report into AI and saying "summarize this." Summaries are where it gets lazy. You get back a paragraph anyone could have written.

Ask it this way instead. Drop in the filing (or the earnings call transcript), then copy this:

"The document you have is the [company + which quarter] report. Answer three questions in order. For every one, point to the exact section or line item you are quoting; if you cannot find it, say 'this document does not contain that' and do not speculate.
1. Compared with last quarter, which three numbers moved the most? Better or worse, and what reason does the document itself give?
2. Compared with last quarter, where did management's wording get more cautious and where did it get more optimistic? Paste both original sentences side by side.
3. Which passage in this document is easiest to skip past but could work against the next few quarters? Why?
Then add one line: what would we have to see for the concern in question 3 to be confirmed, or cleared?"

Four reasons this works:
1. Demanding a citation raises the cost of making things up — it has to point at an actual passage.
2. Letting it say "not in this document" is the important one. Take away its room to admit it does not know and it will invent something for you.
3. Asking which words changed since last quarter catches tone shifts, which usually show up before the numbers do — and that comparison is the most tedious job for a human and the one AI is best at.
4. The last question turns the conclusion into something that can be knocked down, instead of a book report.

Three warnings:
- Check every number it gives you against the original filing yourself. It still makes things up.
- One quarter shows no trend. Feed it the last two or three before you ask question 1.
- This is for understanding what a company is saying, not a call to buy or sell anything. It does not know your cost basis or how long you plan to hold.

Same discipline — get what matters sorted first, then judge for yourself — done for you every morning: in your inbox by 7:00am, Monday through Saturday, with the index, the sectors and what to watch today for the companies you follow (up to 80 of them), plus an AI assistant for whatever you still do not get, 30 messages a day.
